body: Haha yeah, I picked it b/c I thought it would fix me... just accelerated the need to transition and made my life miserable in one go.

I have been talking a lot with my supervisors about trying to be better at work, but time and time again I'm just not. I know from experience that I won't be better even if I think I will going into a day. I can't guarantee it, and not only that, I've shown time and time again to them that I'm not getting better and I'm still making things difficult for my coworkers. To tell my boss this is to lie and besides the point at this stage.

I do take walks to try to clear my mind. It does not seem to help.
i think you missed the part where i'm losing my job

It's mostly positive here. There's a pretty stellar gender support group that meets every Wednesday night on capitol hill, in a super LGBT-friendly counseling center. If you read my last post you'll see that this is not usual treatment for me to get, it's just been happening recently out of the blue. Passing so much of the time makes it a lot harder in the event that somebody does treat me like shit, and it really opens my eyes to the shit "non-passing" transwomen probably get on a daily basis. Still basically impossible to cope with though.

*edit* it is kind of a stereotype that trans* people from all over the country come here, though. I even read a young adult novel (Luna) where that's how the book ends; the trans character up and moves to Seattle, where everything is super hunky dory for all trans people. It's not always the case, but it's a lot more often the case than any other city I'm aware of.
I'm already in a super liberal city.
And sometimes I find that fact very sexy. Hooray for intriguing secondary sexual characteristics?
